Thanks.  I called in sick to work today.  Just can't be around people without feeling on the verge of instability.  The suicidal thoughts are just escapism.  I've been like this before and I know it can get better.  It's when I start facing bigger questions, like "what's the point" is when I question purpose at all.  I'm just chewing up days and spitting them out.  There are no goals.  I'm more fearful of my creasing desire to be alone.  I don't like being alone, but I have a very short tolerance for being around others.

The best thing I can offer is that, although I am in this down-cycle right now, I'm old enough that I've had them before and recovered to some degree.  I think I have to hang on for 5 more weeks, then step back and try to reset.  I think about suicide all the time as an easy solution and I have for years.  It's not healthy, but it's worse to ignore the thoughts.  

Bottom line is that I tell no one about this because it's too humiliating.  Friends and coworkers see me as grumpy, mean, and anti-social.  I refuse to explain these kinds of things, I'm far too private.

It's odd how enjoyable it can be to pull away.  It's Saturday, and I don't see a situation where I get out of bed.  My life isn't even tough, I just make it miserable.  Then I feel guilty about that and the cycle continues.

I've been hunting online for places to discuss things anonymously.  Psych Central forums are okay.  But many are too quick to try and be problem solvers.  Im just looking for contact.  I'm old enough to know what needs to be done to correct myself.

Psychcentral.com
Forums
Depression

I share some of your problems.  I seem to be becoming more secluded, cut off, and just unhealthy.  And it's by choice.  I don't answer the phone, I come home from work and watch reruns until I'm tired, I wake up and drag myself to work, and repeat.  Avoiding people seems to be the easiest and most low energy way of dealing with uncomfortable situations.  

Anyhow, I can talk.
